title: The forward Roos subsequence transition and its explicit homotopy
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring and $\mathcal A$ the abelian category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Let $K_\bullet$ be a strict tower of cochain complexes with transitions $t_i:K_{i+1}\to K_i$, $i\ge1$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Write $T_{n,i}=t_n\cdots t_{i-1}:K_i\to K_n$ for $i\ge n$, with $T_{n,n}=1$, and put $U=\prod_nK_n$, $(sx)_n=t_nx_{n+1}$, $f=1-s$. Use
$$\mathsf R(K)=\operatorname{Cone}(f:U\to U)[-1],\quad\mathsf R(K)^q=U^{q-1}\oplus U^q,\quad d(y,x)=(-dy-fx,dx)$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an integer $e\ge1$ let $K^{(e)}_n=K_{en}$ with composite transitions. Define the product maps
$$a_e(x)_n=x_{en},\qquad b_e(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{en,i}y_i,\qquad T(z)_n=T_{n,en}z_n.$$
The first two maps induce $r_e(y,x)=(b_ey,a_ex):\mathsf R(K)\to\mathsf R(K^{(e)})$. The last induces a chain map $\Delta(y,x)=(Ty,Tx):\mathsf R(K^{(e)})\to\mathsf R(K)$. Put
$$\varphi(x)_n=T_{n,en}x_{en},\qquad\psi(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i,\qquad h(y)_n=\sum_{i=n}^{en-1}T_{n,i}y_i.$$
Then $\Delta r_e=(\psi,\varphi)$, $hf=1-\varphi$ and $fh=1-\psi$. The degree $-1$ map $H(y,x)=(0,-hy)$ is a chain homotopy satisfying $dH+Hd=1-\Delta r_e$ for the displayed shifted-cone convention. Consequently $\Delta$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $[\Delta]=[r_e]^{-1}$ in the derived category. These identities are natural for morphisms of strict towers. If the $K_i$ are also modules over a sheaf of commutative $\underline A$-algebras $\mathcal R$ and their transitions are $\mathcal R$-linear, every displayed map and the homotopy is $\mathcal R$-linear, and the same quasi-isomorphism and localized inverse identity hold in $D(\mathcal R)$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), Roos model; agent-formulated forward transition and homotopy extracted from returned proof Step 7, Cofinality and Coordinate check. The explicit homotopy is not a literal assertion of Tag 0941.

proof.text:
All coordinate formulas are identities of morphisms after projection to each product factor, not an assumption that cohomology is computed sectionwise. By [def-weil-inverse-system], $T_{a,b}T_{b,c}=T_{a,c}$ and $dT_{a,b}=T_{a,b}d$. By the universal property in [def-weil-category-product], each displayed finite sum of composites with projections defines a unique product map. Each commutes with $d$, since every summand does. Write $V=\prod_nK_{en}$, $(s_ez)_n=T_{en,e(n+1)}z_{n+1}$ and $f_e=1-s_e$. The equality
$$(sTz)_n=t_nT_{n+1,e(n+1)}z_{n+1}=T_{n,e(n+1)}z_{n+1}=(Ts_ez)_n$$
gives $fT=Tf_e$. The cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] now gives $d(Ty,Tx)=(-Tdy-Tf_ex,Tdx)=\Delta d(y,x)$, so $\Delta$ is a chain map.

proof.text:
Compute the square for the other comparison, using $T_{en,i}t_i=T_{en,i+1}$:
$$(b_efx)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}(T_{en,i}x_i-T_{en,i+1}x_{i+1})=x_{en}-T_{en,e(n+1)}x_{e(n+1)}=(f_ea_ex)_n.$$
Successive intermediate terms cancel, including when $e=1$, when the block has one term. Thus $b_ef=f_ea_e$. Substitution in the shifted-cone differential gives
$$d(b_ey,a_ex)=(-b_edy-b_efx,a_edx)=r_ed(y,x).$$
This proves that $r_e$ is the stated chain map, with different maps on the two coordinates.

proof.text:
The composites on the two product coordinates are
$$(Ta_ex)_n=T_{n,en}x_{en}=\varphi(x)_n,$$
$$(Tb_ey)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,en}T_{en,i}y_i=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i=\psi(y)_n.$$
Consequently $\Delta r_e(y,x)=(\psi y,\varphi x)$. These are componentwise product identities by [def-weil-category-product].

proof.text:
The first telescoping identity is
$$(hfx)_n=\sum_{i=n}^{en-1}(T_{n,i}x_i-T_{n,i+1}x_{i+1})=x_n-T_{n,en}x_{en}.$$
It follows that $hf=1-\varphi$. For $e=1$ this sum is empty and its right side is also zero; otherwise the cancellation is the same adjacent-term cancellation as in Step 2. This uses only composition of the transitions of [def-weil-inverse-system].

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), Roos model; explicit finite-block computation by Q41, not an assertion quoted from that lemma

proof.text:
For the other identity subtract the two finite intervals:
$$(fhy)_n=\sum_{i=n}^{en-1}T_{n,i}y_i-\sum_{i=n+1}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i
=y_n-\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i.$$
The equality follows by adding $\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i$ to the first sum: their joined interval is $[n,e(n+1))$, and removing $[n+1,e(n+1))$ leaves only the $n$th term. This also handles $en=n$ without an overlap assumption. Hence $fh=1-\psi$.

proof.text:
Because $dh=hd$, the degree $-1$ map $H(y,x)=(0,-hy)$ satisfies, in the displayed convention,
$$dH(y,x)=(fhy,-dhy),\qquad Hd(y,x)=(0,hdy+hfx).$$
Their sum is $(fhy,hfx)=((1-\psi)y,(1-\varphi)x)=(1-\Delta r_e)(y,x)$. This explicitly verifies both the negative sign in $H$ and the negative signs in the first component of the shifted-cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), Roos model; explicit finite-block computation by Q41, not an assertion quoted from that lemma

proof.text:
We also need the opposite composite, rather than inferring invertibility from just one homotopy. Put $L_n=K_{en}$ and $S_{a,b}=T_{ea,eb}$. Direct substitution gives
$$(r_e\Delta)(y,x)_n=\left(\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{en,ei}y_i,\ T_{en,e^2n}x_{en}\right).$$
These are exactly $(\psi_Ly,\varphi_Lx)$, where $\psi_L,\varphi_L$ are the formulas of Step 3 with transitions $S$. Define
$$(h_Ly)_n=\sum_{i=n}^{en-1}S_{n,i}y_i,\qquad G(y,x)=(0,-h_Ly).$$
The cancellations of Steps 4 and 5, with $S$ in place of $T$, give $h_Lf_e=1-\varphi_L$ and $f_eh_L=1-\psi_L$. Expanding as in Step 6 gives $dG+Gd=1-r_e\Delta$. This repeats the already proved finite-sum identities for the tower $L$; it does not assume the lemma being proved for $L$.

proof.text: For completeness, a difference $u-v=dB+Bd$ induces zero on cohomology: on $Z^q=\ker d^q$ the term $Bd$ vanishes, and $dB$ factors through the boundary subobject $\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$, so it is zero in $H^q=Z^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This is the elementary kernel-and-image argument for Stacks Tag 00LR (algebra.tex, lemma-homotopic-equal-homology), and applies in the abelian sheaf category itself. Apply it to $H$ and $G$: $H^q(\Delta)H^q(r_e)=1$ and $H^q(r_e)H^q(\Delta)=1$. Thus each $H^q(\Delta)$ is an isomorphism with inverse $H^q(r_e)$, so $\Delta$ and $r_e$ are quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00LR (lemma-homotopic-equal-homology); elementary kernel/image proof supplied here for the abelian category of sheaves

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the localization can equivalently be taken from the homotopy category, so the two homotopies already proved imply $[\Delta][r_e]=1$ and $[r_e][\Delta]=1$. Alternatively the cohomology calculation in Step 8 makes both arrows invertible at localization. Therefore $[\Delta]=[r_e]^{-1}$. No identification with an unspecified cofinality isomorphism is involved: these are the images of the specified chain maps.

proof.text:
Let $u_i:K_i\to K'_i$ be a strict tower morphism. Repeatedly using $u_it_i=t'_iu_{i+1}$ gives $u_aT_{a,b}=T'_{a,b}u_b$. Thus, with $P(u)=\prod_i u_i$ and $P_e(u)=\prod_nu_{en}$,
$$P_e(u)a_e=a'_eP(u),\quad P_e(u)b_e=b'_eP(u),\quad P(u)T=T'P_e(u),\quad P(u)h=h'P(u).$$
Each equality follows by substituting the preceding transition identity into each finite summand. They prove naturality of $r_e,\Delta,\varphi,\psi$ and $H$ (and likewise $G$). If the tower is a tower of $\mathcal R$-module complexes, projections and transitions are $\mathcal R$-linear; their composites and finite sums remain $\mathcal R$-linear by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Explicitly, on an object $W$ of the site set $P(W)=\prod_i K_i(W)$, with restrictions and $\mathcal R(W)$-action componentwise. A matching family in $P$ glues uniquely in each $K_i$, hence uniquely in $P$; so $P$ is a sheaf. Coordinatewise lifting gives exactly the product universal property in [def-weil-category-product]. Thus these products exist in the $\mathcal R$-module category and the same formulas define maps there. Repeat Steps 1–9 there to obtain the quasi-isomorphism and localized inverse identity in $D(\mathcal R)$. This repetition needs existence of products, but not exactness of products of $\mathcal R$-modules; no derived-product claim was used.
